problem.title_as_question: Why shouldn't the racket go directly towards the ball on the forehand?
problem.definition: Directing the racket straight towards the ball prematurely reduces shot velocity and turns the forehand stroke into a volley-like push.

symptoms.description: The forehand lacks velocity and mimics a push volley.
The racket moves directly towards the ball upon initial release instead of moving outward.

causes.statement: The player directs the racket straight towards the ball upon release instead of moving outward, preventing proper shoulder adduction for velocity.

angles.summary: Releasing the racket outward first positions the arm properly so the shoulder can adduct powerfully through the ball.
Moving directly towards the ball is appropriate for a volley where velocity is not needed, but incorrect for a forehand.

solutions.summary: Focus on making the first vector of the swing go outward before adducting the shoulder through the ball.
